questions.question: Explain how and why Islam spread into West Africa from about the ninth century.
questions.expected_answer: It spread mainly peacefully through Muslim traders who crossed the Sahara and settled in Sahel trading towns. West African merchants converted because shared faith built trust, allowed credit and partnerships, provided common laws for contracts, and gave access to a wide Muslim trading network. Rulers followed, gaining literate advisers and diplomatic links.

questions.question: Describe three changes Islam brought to West African towns.
questions.expected_answer: Literacy in the Arabic script (and Ajami for local languages); Quranic schools and advanced scholarship; scholars as advisers, secretaries and judges (qadis) using Islamic law; written records for trade and government; mud-brick mosques; links with the wider Muslim world through study and pilgrimage.

questions.question: Why must historians be careful when using Ibn Battuta's description of Mali as evidence?
questions.expected_answer: He was an outsider, a strict Muslim scholar from Morocco, who judged Mali by his own standards; his criticism of court customs reflects his own views. His account is valuable as an eyewitness primary source but may be biased, so it should be compared with other sources such as oral traditions and archaeology.
